blocks.path: Red eye
s: A red eye is usually nothing to worry about and often gets better on its own.
But sometimes it can be serious and you'll need to get medical help.

blocks.path: Red eye > Common causes of a red eye
s: A red eye is often caused by an infection or dry eyes, but there are lots of possible causes.

blocks.path: Red eye > Common causes of a red eye
s: Do not try to diagnose it yourself.

blocks.path: Red eye > Common causes of a red eye
s: Symptoms | Possible cause

blocks.path: Red eye > Common causes of a red eye
s: Bright red area in the white of your eye | Burst blood vessel

blocks.path: Red eye > Common causes of a red eye
s: Gritty or burning feeling, sticky eyes | Conjunctivitis

blocks.path: Red eye > Common causes of a red eye
s: Sore, blurry or watery eyes | Dry eyes

blocks.path: Red eye > Common causes of a red eye
s: Itchy, sore or red crusted eyelids | Blepharitis

blocks.path: Red eye > Common causes of a red eye
s: Feels like there's something in your eye or there is a problem with your eyelashes | Ingrowing eyelash

blocks.path: Red eye > Common causes of a red eye
s: Swollen, drooping or twitching eyelid, or a lump on your eyelid | Eyelid problems

blocks.path: Red eye > What to do if you have a red eye
s: If your eye does not hurt, your sight is not affected and you do not feel sick or unwell, it's probably nothing serious.
It may get better on its own in a few days.

blocks.path: Red eye > What to do if you have a red eye
s: Until it has got better:

blocks.path: Red eye > What to do if you have a red eye
s: try not to touch or rub your eye

blocks.path: Red eye > What to do if you have a red eye
s: do not wear contact lenses

blocks.path: Red eye > What to do if you have a red eye > A pharmacist can help if you have a red eye
s: You can ask a pharmacist if:

blocks.path: Red eye > What to do if you have a red eye > A pharmacist can help if you have a red eye
s: there's anything you can do to treat your eye yourself

blocks.path: Red eye > What to do if you have a red eye > A pharmacist can help if you have a red eye
s: you can buy anything to help, such as cleaning solutions, eyedrops or medicines

blocks.path: Red eye > What to do if you have a red eye > A pharmacist can help if you have a red eye
s: you need to see a GP or optician

blocks.path: Red eye > Non-urgent advice: See a GP or optician if:
s: your child is under 2 years old and has a red eye

blocks.path: Red eye > Non-urgent advice: See a GP or optician if:
s: you have red eyes with a sticky discharge

blocks.path: Red eye > Non-urgent advice: See a GP or optician if:
s: you have red patches in your eye or a problem with your eyelids or eyelashes for more than a few days

blocks.path: Red eye > Non-urgent advice: See a GP or optician if:
s: you're worried about your eyes

blocks.path: Red eye > Non-urgent advice: See a GP or optician if:
s: If the GP or optician cannot find what's causing your red eye, they may refer you to an eye specialist (ophthalmologist) for tests.

blocks.path: Red eye > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent appointment with a GP or optician, or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: your baby has red eyes and they're less than 28 days old

blocks.path: Red eye > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent appointment with a GP or optician, or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: your eye is very painful and red

blocks.path: Red eye > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent appointment with a GP or optician, or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you have a red eye and wear contact lenses – you could have an eye infection

blocks.path: Red eye > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent appointment with a GP or optician, or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: You can call 111 or get help from 111 online.

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: You have a red eye and:

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you have any changes to your sight, like wavy lines, flashing or loss of vision

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: it hurts to look at light

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you have a severe headache and feel sick

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: your eye or eyes are very dark red

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you have injured your eye, or something is stuck in your eye (such as a piece of glass or grit)

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: your eye injury was caused by a dangerous liquid, such as a chemical

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: 1 pupil is bigger than the other

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Do not drive to A&E. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 and ask for an ambulance.

blocks.path: Red eye > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Bring any medicines you take with you.
